source.text: Ταῦτα εἰπὼν Ἰησοῦς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ πέραν τοῦ χειμάρρου τοῦ Κεδρὼν ὅπου ἦν κῆπος, εἰς ὃν εἰσῆλθεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: These things having said, Jesus went out with the disciples of him across the winter-stream of the Kidron, where was a garden, into which entered he and the disciples of him.

en.L: Having said these things, Jesus went out with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples across the winter stream of the Kidron, where there was a garden, into which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples entered.
en.B: When Jesus had said these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and crossed the Kidron Valley. A garden was there, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples went into it.
en.R: When Jesus had finished praying, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left the city with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and crossed over the Kidron Valley. On the other side there was a garden, and Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples went into it.

fr.L: Ayant dit ces choses, Jésus sortit avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples au-delà du torrent du Cédron, où il y avait un jardin, dans lequel entrèrent {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.B: Quand Jésus eut dit ces choses, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et traversa la vallée du Cédron. Il y avait là un jardin, où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.R: Quand Jésus a eu fini de prier, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a quitté la ville avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a traversé la vallée du Cédron. De l’autre côté, il y avait un jardin, et Jésus y est entré avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.

vi.L: Sau khi nói những điều này, Đức Giê-xu đi ra với các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sang bên kia khe suối mùa đông Xết-rôn, nơi có một khu vườn mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi vào.
vi.B: Nói xong những điều này, Đức Giê-xu đi ra cùng các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và băng qua thung lũng Xết-rôn. Ở đó có một khu vườn, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng các môn đồ vào vườn ấy.
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu cầu nguyện xong, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng các môn đồ ra khỏi thành và đi qua thung lũng Xết-rôn. Bên kia thung lũng có một khu vườn, và Đức Giê-xu cùng các môn đồ đi vào đó.

ko.L: 예수께서 이것들을 말씀하시고 나서, 그분의 제자들과 함께 기드론 겨울 시내 건너편으로 나가셨다. 그곳에 동산이 있었는데, 그분과 그분의 제자들이 그 안으로 들어갔다.
ko.B: 예수께서 이 말씀을 하신 뒤에 제자들과 함께 나가서 기드론 골짜기를 건너가셨다. 그곳에 동산이 있었는데, 예수께서 제자들과 함께 그 안으로 들어가셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 기도를 마치시고 제자들과 함께 성을 나가셨다. 그리고 기드론 골짜기를 건너가셨다. 건너편에 동산이 하나 있었는데, 예수께서 제자들과 함께 그리로 들어가셨다.

decisions.choice: having said these things: after the prayer of chapter 17, Jesus leaves for the place of his arrest
alternatives: after the farewell words of chapters 13-17 as a whole
decisions.reason: "These things" points back to what Jesus has just said, the prayer of chapter 17, which closes the words he spoke to his disciples at the supper (13:31-17:26). In 14:31 he had said, "Rise, let us go from here"; only now does John tell of their going out, from the house where they ate and out of the city.

decisions.choice: the winter stream of the Kidron: the valley east of Jerusalem, whose stream flows only in the rainy season
alternatives: a river that flows all year
decisions.reason: The word χειμάρρου means a stream that runs in winter, when the rains come, and is dry for the rest of the year; it is used of the valley it runs through. The Kidron Valley lies between the eastern wall of Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives. At Passover, in spring, it may have held little water. King David crossed the Kidron when he fled from Jerusalem, betrayed by his counselor (2 Samuel 15:23, 31); John does not draw attention to that.

decisions.choice: a garden: an enclosed plot, probably of olive trees, on the slope of the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: John says only "a garden". Matthew and Mark name the place Gethsemane (Matthew 26:36; Mark 14:32), a name meaning "oil press", and Luke places it on the Mount of Olives (Luke 22:39). John will also place Jesus's tomb in a garden (19:41).

decisions.choice: of the Kidron, the name of the valley (SBLGNT)
alternatives: of the cedars (many manuscripts, among them some of the oldest)
decisions.reason: The name Kidron sounds like the Greek word for cedar, and many manuscripts, some of them early, read "the winter stream of the cedars". The SBLGNT reads the place name, which is certainly what is meant: the valley is called the Kidron in the Old Testament (2 Samuel 15:23; 1 Kings 15:13). A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the winter stream of the Kidron (L); the Kidron Valley (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word for a seasonal stream (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable name the valley, which is what a reader can picture and find on a map, since the stream was dry for much of the year.

decisions.choice: had finished praying; left the city; On the other side
alternatives: having said these things; went out (Literal)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "these things" were (the prayer just ended, meaning decision m1) and where Jesus went out from. "On the other side" gives the sense of "across" in a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("il vient", "il dit", verses 3-5); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (18:1-14), as in 1:19. Literal keeps the historic present where John uses it, as the English Literal does; Balanced narrates in the passé simple ("sortit", "arrêtèrent"), the tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé ("a quitté", "ont arrêté"). Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("je vous ai dit").

decisions.choice: le torrent du Cédron (L); la vallée du Cédron (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Torrent" is the French word for a stream that runs only after rain, the sense of the Greek (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable name the valley that Jesus crossed, as the English does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect is carried by the honorific -si-, 께서 and 그분 at every level (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: 기드론 겨울 시내 (L); 기드론 골짜기 (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "winter stream", a brook that runs only in the rainy season; Balanced and Readable name the valley, as the English does.

source.text: ᾔδει δὲ καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν τὸν τόπον, ὅτι πολλάκις συνήχθη Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖ μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Knew now also Judas, the [one] handing over him, the place, because often gathered Jesus there with the disciples of him.

en.L: Now Judas also, the one who was handing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over, knew the place, because Jesus had often gathered there with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.
en.B: Judas, who was betraying {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, also knew the place, since Jesus had often met there with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.
en.R: Judas, the one who was betraying Jesus, knew this place too, because Jesus had often met there with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.

fr.L: Or Judas aussi, celui qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livrait, connaissait l’endroit, parce que Jésus s’y était souvent réuni avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.B: Judas, qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trahissait, connaissait lui aussi l’endroit, car Jésus s’y était souvent retrouvé avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.R: Judas, celui qui trahissait Jésus, connaissait lui aussi cet endroit, parce que Jésus y était souvent venu avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.

vi.L: Vả, Giu-đa, kẻ đang nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, cũng biết chỗ ấy, vì Đức Giê-xu thường nhóm họp tại đó với các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Giu-đa, kẻ phản bội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, cũng biết chỗ này, vì Đức Giê-xu thường họp với các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở đó.
vi.R: Giu-đa, kẻ đang phản bội Đức Giê-xu, cũng biết chỗ này, vì Đức Giê-xu thường gặp các môn đồ ở đó.

ko.L: 그런데 그분을 넘겨주는 자인 유다도 그곳을 알고 있었다. 예수께서 자주 그분의 제자들과 함께 그곳에 모이셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수를 배반하던 유다도 그곳을 알고 있었다. 예수께서 제자들과 함께 자주 그곳에 모이셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 예수님을 배반하던 유다도 그곳을 알고 있었다. 예수께서 제자들과 자주 그곳에서 만나셨기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: the one handing him over: betraying him, and doing it now
alternatives: the one who would later hand him over
decisions.reason: As in 6:64 and 6:71, the verb means to hand someone over, and for Judas it means betrayal. Here the participle is present: the betrayal is already under way. Judas left the supper to do it (13:27-30).

decisions.choice: had often gathered there: the garden was a regular meeting place
decisions.reason: The adverb means "often", and the verb is the ordinary one for coming together. Luke says Jesus went to the Mount of Olives "as was his custom" (Luke 22:39; compare 21:37). Because it was their habit, Judas knew where to find him at night, away from the crowds.

decisions.choice: handing over (L); betraying (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:64 and 6:71 (rendering decision r-en-1 there): Literal keeps the plain sense of the verb, so that the reader sees it is the word later used of the authorities and of Pilate (18:30, 35; 19:16); Balanced and Readable say what Judas's handing over was (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: 넘겨주다 (L); 배반하다 (B, R) for paradidōmi
decisions.reason: As earlier in the book (6:64; 13:2; 13:21): Literal keeps the Greek verb, Balanced and Readable say what Judas was doing.

source.text: ὁ οὖν Ἰούδας λαβὼν τὴν σπεῖραν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων ὑπηρέτας ἔρχεται ἐκεῖ μετὰ φανῶν καὶ λαμπάδων καὶ ὅπλων.

records.literal_gloss: So the Judas, having taken the cohort and from the chief priests and from the Pharisees officers, comes there with lanterns and torches and weapons.

en.L: So Judas, having taken the cohort and officers from the chief priests and from the Pharisees, comes there with lanterns and torches and weapons.
en.B: So Judas went there, bringing the detachment of soldiers and temple police sent by the chief priests and the Pharisees. They carried lanterns, torches and weapons.
en.R: So Judas led a group of Roman soldiers to the garden. Temple guards sent by the leading priests and the Pharisees came with them. They brought lanterns, torches and weapons.

fr.L: Judas donc, ayant pris la cohorte et des gardes de la part des chefs des prêtres et des Pharisiens, vient là avec des lanternes et des torches et des armes.
fr.B: Judas se rendit donc là, emmenant le détachement de soldats et des gardes du temple envoyés par les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens. Ils avaient des lanternes, des torches et des armes.
fr.R: Judas a donc conduit au jardin un groupe de soldats romains. Des gardes du temple, envoyés par les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens, venaient avec eux. Ils avaient apporté des lanternes, des torches et des armes.

vi.L: Vậy Giu-đa, đem theo đội quân và các cảnh vệ từ các thầy tế lễ cả và từ những người Pha-ri-si, đến đó với đèn lồng, đuốc và vũ khí.
vi.B: Vậy Giu-đa dẫn một toán lính cùng lính canh đền thờ do các thầy tế lễ cả và người Pha-ri-si sai đến, kéo tới đó. Họ mang theo đèn lồng, đuốc và vũ khí.
vi.R: Vậy Giu-đa dẫn một toán lính La Mã đến khu vườn. Đi cùng họ có lính canh đền thờ do các thầy tế lễ đứng đầu và người Pha-ri-si sai đến. Họ mang theo đèn lồng, đuốc và vũ khí.

ko.L: 그래서 유다가 부대와, 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들에게서 [온] 경비병들을 데리고, 등불과 횃불과 무기를 가지고 그곳으로 온다.
ko.B: 그래서 유다는 로마 군인 한 부대와, 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들이 보낸 성전 경비병들을 데리고 그곳으로 갔다. 그들은 등불과 횃불과 무기를 들고 있었다.
ko.R: 그래서 유다는 로마 군인들을 이끌고 동산으로 왔다. 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들이 보낸 성전 경비병들도 함께 왔다. 그들은 등불과 횃불과 무기를 들고 있었다.

decisions.choice: the cohort: a unit of Roman soldiers from the garrison in Jerusalem; John need not mean the whole unit
alternatives: the temple guard, called by a military word
the whole cohort, several hundred men
decisions.reason: The word σπεῖραν is the usual term for a Roman cohort, at full strength up to about 600 men, and in 18:12 its commander is called by the title of a Roman tribune. Acts uses the same two words for the Roman garrison in Jerusalem, which was on watch at the festivals, when crowds filled the city (Acts 21:31-32). The article may simply name the unit the soldiers came from; a detachment, not all of it, is the likely meaning. John does not say how the Roman soldiers came to be sent; their presence shows that the Roman authorities were involved from the arrest on. The other Gospels speak of a crowd sent by the chief priests (Mark 14:43).

decisions.choice: officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees: the temple police, sent by the council
decisions.reason: These are the officers who kept order in the temple for the chief priests, sent once before to arrest Jesus and come back without him (7:32, 45-46). The chief priests and the Pharisees are the leaders who met in council and gave orders for his arrest (11:47, 57).

decisions.choice: having taken: Judas brought them and guided them to the place
alternatives: Judas was in command of them
decisions.reason: Judas did not command Roman soldiers or the temple police. He took them along as the one who knew the place (verse 2); Acts 1:16 calls him "guide to those who arrested Jesus".

decisions.choice: lanterns, torches and weapons: equipment for a search at night, and for resistance
decisions.reason: A lantern held a small oil lamp shielded from the wind; a torch was a burning brand. Passover fell at the full moon, but they came prepared to search a dark garden among trees, and armed in case Jesus's followers fought.

decisions.choice: comes (L); went, led (B, R); also says (L), asked and said (B, R) in verses 4 and 5
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense ("he comes", "he says") to make a scene vivid. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told. This applies to every such verb in the passage ("comes" in verse 3, "says" in verses 4 and 5).

decisions.choice: the detachment of soldiers, temple police (B); a group of Roman soldiers, temple guards, leading priests (R)
decisions.reason: "Cohort" names a Roman unit that few readers know, so Balanced says "detachment of soldiers" and Readable says plainly whose soldiers they were (meaning decision m1). The officers are named as at 7:32 and 7:45: "temple police" at Balanced, "temple guards" at Readable (meaning decision m2). Readable says "leading priests", as in John 7 and 11, and splits the long sentence.

decisions.choice: la cohorte (L), le détachement de soldats (B), des soldats romains (R); des gardes (L), des gardes du temple (B, R); les chefs des prêtres (every level)
decisions.reason: As the English (meaning decisions m1 and m2): "cohorte" names the Roman unit at Literal, and Balanced and Readable say what it was. The officers are "gardes", the word used for them through John; "chefs des prêtres" is the book-wide French for the chief priests, kept distinct from "le grand prêtre" (verse 10).

decisions.choice: đội quân, cảnh vệ (L); toán lính, lính canh đền thờ (B); toán lính La Mã, lính canh đền thờ (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used elsewhere in the Vietnamese John (7:32, 7:45) for the temple police; "đội quân" at Literal names the Roman unit, "toán lính" says a detachment of it. Literal keeps the historic present "đến" (comes) by leaving out "đã", as through this passage.

decisions.choice: Historic present kept at Literal (온다, 말씀하신다); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: John tells these steps in the present; Literal keeps it, Balanced and Readable use the narrative past (one decision for the passage).

decisions.choice: 부대, 경비병들 (L); 로마 군인 한 부대, 성전 경비병들 (B); 로마 군인들, 성전 경비병들 (R)
decisions.reason: 부대 is a unit of soldiers without naming its size; the officers were the temple police, and 경비병 says that in modern Korean, where the older 하속 is no longer understood.

source.text: Ἰησοῦς οὖν εἰδὼς πάντα τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἐξῆλθεν, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τίνα ζητεῖτε;

records.literal_gloss: Jesus therefore, knowing all the things coming upon him, went out, and says to them, "Whom do you seek?"

en.L: So Jesus, knowing all the things that were coming upon {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, went out and says to them, "Whom are you seeking?"
en.B: Jesus knew everything that was about to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out to them and asked, "Who is it you are looking for?"
en.R: Jesus knew everything that was going to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out to meet them and asked, "Who are you looking for?"

fr.L: Jésus donc, sachant tout ce qui venait sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, sortit, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Qui cherchez-vous ? »
fr.B: Jésus savait tout ce qui allait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} arriver ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit donc vers eux et leur demanda : « Qui cherchez-vous ? »
fr.R: Jésus savait tout ce qui allait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} arriver. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est sorti à leur rencontre et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a demandé : « Qui cherchez-vous ? »

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu, biết mọi việc sắp xảy đến cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, đi ra và nói với họ: "Các người tìm ai?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu biết mọi việc sắp xảy đến cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ra và hỏi họ: "Các người tìm ai?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu biết mọi việc sắp xảy ra cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vì thế {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ra gặp họ và hỏi: "Các người tìm ai?"

ko.L: 그래서 예수께서는 자기에게 닥쳐올 모든 일을 아시고 나가셔서 그들에게 말씀하신다. "너희는 누구를 찾느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서는 자기에게 닥칠 모든 일을 알고 계셨다. 그래서 그들에게 나가셔서 물으셨다. "누구를 찾고 있느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서는 자신에게 일어날 모든 일을 알고 계셨다. 그래서 그들을 맞으러 나가셔서 물으셨다. "누구를 찾느냐?"

decisions.choice: knowing all that was coming upon him: Jesus goes to meet his arrest knowingly and by his own choice
decisions.reason: John has said that Jesus knew his hour had come (13:1) and knew all that the Father had given into his hands (13:3). He is not caught by surprise: he steps forward himself. He had said that no one takes his life from him, but that he lays it down of his own accord (10:18).

decisions.choice: went out: came out of the garden to meet them
alternatives: stepped forward from among his disciples
decisions.reason: In verse 1 Jesus and his disciples went into the garden; now he goes out toward the men coming for him. The word may also mean only that he stepped forward. Either way he meets them before they find him.

decisions.choice: Whom are you seeking?: Jesus makes them name the one they have come for
decisions.reason: "Seek" runs through John's Gospel. Jesus's first words in it are "What are you seeking?" (1:38), and after the resurrection he asks Mary, "Whom are you seeking?" (20:15). Here those who seek him seek to arrest him, as others had sought to kill him (5:18; 7:1, 30). His question leads them to say his name (verse 5).

decisions.choice: went out to them (B); went out to meet them (R); asked (B, R); Who (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom he went out toward (meaning decision m2) and use "asked" for the present "says" before a question (historic present, rendering decision r-en-1 at verse 3). Literal keeps the formal "whom"; Balanced and Readable use everyday "who".

decisions.choice: Qui cherchez-vous ?
decisions.reason: French "chercher" covers both "seek" and "look for", so every level asks the same short question, which keeps the echo of 1:38 and 20:15 and the repetition of verse 7.

decisions.choice: Jesus says "Ta" for himself and "các người" to the arresting party
decisions.reason: The style guide's forms of address: Jesus speaks to opponents and officials as "các người", which keeps distance without contempt.

fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Jésus, celui de Nazareth. »

ko.R: 그들이 대답했다. "나사렛에서 온 예수를 찾고 있다."

decisions.choice: the Nazorean: the man from Nazareth
alternatives: a title with a further meaning, such as a play on the "branch" of Isaiah 11:1
decisions.reason: The word Ναζωραῖος is one of two forms used in the New Testament of Jesus as the man from Nazareth; Mark uses the other (Mark 1:24; 14:67), and both mean the same thing (compare Acts 2:22; 22:8). John uses this form only in the arrest and on the notice over the cross (18:5, 7; 19:19). Nazareth was a small town in Galilee, and Jesus was known by it (1:45-46). Matthew links the name with the words of the prophets (Matthew 2:23); John makes no such link. A footnote gives the form of the word.

decisions.choice: the Nazorean (L); of Nazareth (B); from Nazareth (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the word as a title; Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable leave out "him" after "answered", which English does not need.

decisions.choice: Jésus le Nazôréen (L); de Nazareth (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form John uses (meaning decision m1) in the usual French spelling of scholarly translations, "Nazôréen"; Balanced and Readable say where he was from, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Giê-xu" without the honorific "Đức" in the mouths of the arresting party; Na-xa-rét
decisions.reason: The soldiers and officers do not honour Jesus, so they name him plainly, as the man born blind does before he believes (9:11). "Na-xa-rét" is the established Protestant spelling of Nazareth.

decisions.choice: The arresting party answers Jesus in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: They have come to arrest him and do not treat him as a superior; the guide allows opponents to speak to Jesus without honorifics where the scene is hostile.

decisions.choice: 나사렛 사람 (L); 나사렛 (B); 나사렛에서 온 (R) for "the Nazorean"
decisions.reason: The title means the man from Nazareth; Literal keeps it as a title with 사람.

fr.B: Il leur dit : « Je le suis. »

vi.L: Ngài nói với họ: "Ta là [người đó]."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ta đây."

ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 바로 그 사람이다."

decisions.choice: I am: first of all "I am he", the man you are looking for; the words also echo the way God names himself, which verse 6 brings out
alternatives: the bare "I am", the divine name, as the main sense
only the plain sense, with no echo
decisions.reason: The words have no predicate, but the question supplies one: they are seeking Jesus of Nazareth, and he says he is that man. Verse 8 takes the words up in that sense: "I told you that I am he; so if you are seeking me, let these men go." Yet John repeats the words three times (verses 5, 6 and 8), and when Jesus says them, the men who came to arrest him draw back and fall to the ground (verse 6). "I am" is how God speaks of himself in the Greek of Isaiah (Isaiah 43:10; compare Exodus 3:14), and Jesus has used the words of himself with nothing after them (8:24, 28, 58; 13:19). Here, unlike 8:58, a plain sense fits the words, so it is taken as uppermost, and the echo of God's name is heard within it, as at 6:20. Marked uncertain because the weight between the two senses is a judgment. A footnote gives the bare "I am".

decisions.choice: I am [he] (L); I am he (B, R); also verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: Because the plain sense is uppermost here (meaning decision m1), every level supplies "he", in brackets at Literal as at 6:20, and it takes the deity_pronoun setting as a pronoun for Christ. "I am he" is also the English used for God's words in Isaiah 43:10 and Deuteronomy 32:39, so the echo can still be heard, which "It is I" or "I am the one" would lose. The same words stand at verses 5, 6 and 8 so the reader sees the repetition. "Said" and "told" stand for the present "says" (rendering decision r-en-1 at verse 3). The footnote gives the bare "I am".

decisions.choice: Je [le] suis (L); Je le suis (B); C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} (R); the same in verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m1 takes the plain sense, "I am the man you seek", as uppermost, with an echo of God's name. French "Je le suis" gives that sense while keeping the words "je ... suis" visible, so the repetition and the link with 8:24, 8:28, 8:58 and 13:19 can still be seen; Literal brackets the "le" that the Greek lacks. Here "le" stands for the predicate ("Jésus le Nazôréen"), not for a person, so unlike the English "he" it takes no deity_pronoun setting. Readable says "C’est moi", the everyday answer, where the pronoun for Jesus does take the setting. The footnote of m1 gives the bare "Je suis".

decisions.choice: Ta là [người đó] (L); Chính Ta đây (B); Ta đây (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot leave "I am" without a complement, so the bare words that echo God's name cannot be kept; the meaning decision's footnote gives that echo. "Ta đây" (here I am) is how a person answers to his name, and "chính" stresses that he is the very one. Also verses 6 and 8.

decisions.choice: 내가 [그 사람]이다 (L); 내가 그 사람이다 (B); 내가 바로 그 사람이다 (R) for egō eimi, also in verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: Korean must say who "I am" is, so the plain sense the English follows is given; the echo of God's name cannot be kept in Korean wording and is left to the meaning note and its footnote.

source.text: εἱστήκει δὲ καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν μετ’ αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Had stood now also Judas, the [one] handing over him, with them.

en.L: And Judas also, the one handing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over, was standing with them.
en.B: Judas, who was betraying {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, was standing there with them.
en.R: Judas, the one who was betraying Jesus, was standing there with them.

fr.L: Or Judas aussi, celui qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livrait, se tenait avec eux.
fr.B: Judas, qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trahissait, se tenait là avec eux.
fr.R: Judas, celui qui trahissait Jésus, était là avec eux.

vi.L: Và Giu-đa, kẻ nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, cũng đứng với họ.
vi.B: Giu-đa, kẻ phản bội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, cũng đang đứng đó với họ.
vi.R: Giu-đa, kẻ phản bội Đức Giê-xu, cũng đang đứng đó với họ.

ko.L: 그리고 그분을 넘겨주는 자인 유다도 그들과 함께 서 있었다.
ko.B: 예수를 배반하던 유다도 그들과 함께 서 있었다.
ko.R: 예수님을 배반하던 유다도 그들과 함께 거기 서 있었다.

decisions.choice: Judas was standing with them: the disciple now stands with those who have come to arrest Jesus
decisions.reason: John places Judas among the arresting party at the moment Jesus names himself. The one Jesus chose as one of the Twelve (6:70-71), who ate bread with him (13:18, 26), now stands on the other side. The verb is pluperfect in form, "had taken his stand", but in this verb that form means simply "was standing".

decisions.choice: the one handing him over: betraying him
decisions.reason: The same present participle as in verse 2 (meaning decision m1 there): the betrayal is happening as John tells it.

decisions.choice: handing over (L); betraying (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2 (rendering decision r-en-1 there). Readable names Jesus, so that "him" is not taken to mean someone in the arresting party.

source.text: ὡς οὖν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγώ εἰμι, ἀπῆλθον εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καὶ ἔπεσαν χαμαί.

records.literal_gloss: When therefore he said to them, "I am," they went away into the [places] behind and fell to-ground.

en.L: So when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "I am [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}]," they went backward and fell to the ground.
en.B: When Jesus said to them, "I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}," they stepped backward and fell to the ground.
en.R: When Jesus said, "I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}," they moved back and fell down on the ground.

fr.L: Lors donc qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Je [le] suis », ils s’en allèrent en arrière et tombèrent à terre.
fr.B: Quand Jésus leur dit : « Je le suis », ils reculèrent et tombèrent à terre.
fr.R: Quand Jésus a dit : « C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} », ils ont fait un pas en arrière et ils sont tombés par terre.

vi.L: Vậy khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Ta là [người đó]," họ lùi lại phía sau và ngã xuống đất.
vi.B: Khi Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đây," họ lùi lại và ngã xuống đất.
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu nói: "Ta đây," họ lùi lại và té xuống đất.

ko.L: 그래서 그분이 그들에게 "내가 [그 사람]이다" 하고 말씀하시자, 그들은 뒤로 물러나 땅에 쓰러졌다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 "내가 그 사람이다" 하고 말씀하시자, 그들은 뒤로 물러서다가 땅에 넘어졌다.
ko.R: 예수께서 "내가 바로 그 사람이다" 하고 말씀하시자, 그들은 뒤로 물러나더니 땅바닥에 쓰러졌다.

decisions.choice: they drew back and fell to the ground: overcome by the one who spoke, they cannot take him until he allows it
alternatives: they stumbled back in surprise or fear, with no further meaning
decisions.reason: John tells it as a direct result of Jesus's words: "when he said ... they drew back and fell". In the Scriptures people fall to the ground before an appearance of God or of his messenger (Ezekiel 1:28; Daniel 10:9; Acts 9:4). The armed men who came to seize Jesus end up on the ground before him; he is arrested only because he gives himself up (10:18; verses 4 and 8).

decisions.choice: possibly the psalms in which the enemies of the righteous are turned back and fall
decisions.reason: Psalm 27:2 says of the psalmist's enemies, "they stumbled and fell", and Psalm 35:4 prays that those who seek his life may be "turned back". John does not quote these psalms, so the echo is uncertain.

decisions.choice: I am: as in verse 5, with the echo of God's name brought out by what follows
decisions.reason: See meaning decision m1 at 18:5. John repeats Jesus's words before telling of the men's fall, which shows that the words themselves, not only the surprise of being met, threw them back.

decisions.choice: I am [he] (L), I am he (B, R); went backward (L), stepped backward (B), moved back (R)
decisions.reason: "I am he" as at verse 5 (rendering decision r-en-1 there). The Greek says they "went away to the things behind", a phrase for moving backward; each level says that in plain words. Balanced and Readable name Jesus as the speaker.

source.text: πάλιν οὖν ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτούς· Τίνα ζητεῖτε;

records.literal_gloss: Again therefore he asked them, "Whom do you seek?"

en.L: So again {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "Whom are you seeking?"
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them again, "Who is it you are looking for?"
en.R: Jesus asked them again, "Who are you looking for?"

fr.L: De nouveau donc, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demanda : « Qui cherchez-vous ? »
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demanda de nouveau : « Qui cherchez-vous ? »
fr.R: Jésus leur a demandé encore une fois : « Qui cherchez-vous ? »

vi.L: Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại hỏi họ: "Các người tìm ai?"
vi.B: Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi họ lần nữa: "Các người tìm ai?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu hỏi họ lần nữa: "Các người tìm ai?"

ko.L: 그래서 그분이 다시 그들에게 물으셨다. "너희는 누구를 찾느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 다시 그들에게 물으셨다. "누구를 찾고 있느냐?"

decisions.choice: he asked them again: Jesus keeps the lead, and makes them name him alone
decisions.reason: The men have fallen to the ground, and it is Jesus, not they, who speaks next. By asking the same question he has them say again that it is Jesus of Nazareth they want, and so he can ask that his disciples go free (verse 8).

decisions.choice: Who is it (B); Who (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4 (rendering decision r-en-1 there). Readable names Jesus, since the men have just been the subject.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον.

fr.L: Et eux dirent : « Jésus le Nazôréen. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu encore : « Jésus, celui de Nazareth. »

vi.R: Họ lại trả lời: "Giê-xu ở Na-xa-rét."

ko.R: 그들이 다시 대답했다. "나사렛에서 온 예수를 찾고 있다."

decisions.choice: they give the same answer: what happened to them does not change their purpose
decisions.reason: Even after falling to the ground before him, they say the same name. John has noted before that signs did not turn Jesus's opponents from their course (11:47-53; 12:37).

decisions.choice: the Nazorean: the man from Nazareth
decisions.reason: As in verse 5 (meaning decision m1 there).

decisions.choice: of Nazareth (B); from Nazareth (R); answered again (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 5 (rendering decision r-en-1 there). Readable adds "again" to show that they repeat their first answer (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Εἶπον ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι· εἰ οὖν ἐμὲ ζητεῖτε, ἄφετε τούτους ὑπάγειν·

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus, "I told you that I am; if therefore me you seek, let these to go away";

en.L: Jesus answered, "I told you that I am [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}]. So if you are seeking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, let these [men] go away."
en.B: Jesus replied, "I have told you that I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}. So if it is {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you are looking for, let these men go."
en.R: "I told you that I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}," Jesus answered. "If I am the one you want, let these men go."

fr.L: Jésus répondit : « Je vous ai dit que je [le] suis ; si donc vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} cherchez, laissez ceux-ci s’en aller. »
fr.B: Jésus répondit : « Je vous ai dit que je le suis. Si c’est donc {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} que vous cherchez, laissez partir ces hommes. »
fr.R: « Je vous ai dit que c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} », a répondu Jésus. « Si c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} que vous voulez, laissez partir ces hommes. »

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ta đã nói với các người rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là [người đó]. Vậy nếu các người tìm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, hãy để những [người] này đi."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Ta đã nói với các người rằng chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đây. Vậy nếu các người tìm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì hãy để những người này đi."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Ta đã nói với các người là {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đây. Nếu các người tìm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì hãy để những người này đi."

ko.L: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "내가 [그 사람]이라고 너희에게 말하였다. 그러니 너희가 나를 찾는다면, 이 [사람들은] 가게 하여라."
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "내가 그 사람이라고 너희에게 말하지 않았느냐. 너희가 찾는 사람이 나라면, 이 사람들은 가게 내버려 두어라."
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "내가 바로 그 사람이라고 말하지 않았느냐? 너희가 찾는 사람이 나라면, 이 사람들은 보내 주어라."

decisions.choice: I am: as in verses 5 and 6; here the plain sense is clear from what follows
decisions.reason: See meaning decision m1 at 18:5. "If you are seeking me" shows that "I am" answered their question: he is the Jesus of Nazareth they seek. The third time, after the men have fallen, the words still carry the echo John has drawn out.

decisions.choice: me ... these: Jesus gives himself up so that his disciples go free
decisions.reason: The pronoun "me" is written out and put first for emphasis, set against "these", the disciples. As the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep and does not leave them to the wolf (10:11-12), Jesus hands himself over and asks for his disciples' safety.

decisions.choice: let these go away: a demand, spoken as one in command of the scene
decisions.reason: The verb is an imperative, "allow them to go". Jesus, the one being arrested, tells the arresting party what to do, and the disciples are not taken (verse 9).

decisions.choice: I am [he] (L), I am he (B, R); these [men] (L), these men (B, R); if it is me (B); If I am the one you want (R)
decisions.reason: "I am he" as at verse 5 (rendering decision r-en-1 there). "These" is masculine plural and means the disciples, so "men" is supplied, in brackets at Literal. Balanced and Readable bring out the stress on "me" (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ἵνα πληρωθῇ ὁ λόγος ὃν εἶπεν ὅτι Οὓς δέδωκάς μοι οὐκ ἀπώλεσα ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐδένα.

records.literal_gloss: So that might be fulfilled the word which he said, "Whom you have given to me, not I lost of them not one."

en.L: [This was] so that the word which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said might be fulfilled, "Those whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I did not lose one of them."
en.B: This was so that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own word would be fulfilled: "I have not lost a single one of those {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: This happened so that what Jesus had said would come true: "I have not lost even one of the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

fr.L: [C’était] afin que soit accomplie la parole qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dite : « Ceux que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donnés, je n’ai perdu aucun d’entre eux. »
fr.B: Cela arriva pour que s’accomplisse {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} propre parole : « Je n’ai perdu aucun de ceux que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donnés. »
fr.R: Cela est arrivé pour que se réalise ce que Jésus avait dit : « Je n’ai perdu aucun de ceux que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donnés, pas même un seul. »

vi.L: [Việc này xảy ra] để lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói được ứng nghiệm: "Những người Cha đã ban cho Con, Con không để mất một ai trong họ."
vi.B: Điều này xảy ra để chính lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói được ứng nghiệm: "Trong những người Cha đã ban cho Con, Con không để mất một ai."
vi.R: Việc này xảy ra để lời Đức Giê-xu đã nói trở thành sự thật: "Con không để mất một ai trong những người Cha đã ban cho Con."

ko.L: [이는] 그분이 "아버지께서 저에게 주신 자들 가운데 저는 하나도 잃지 않았습니다" 하고 하신 말씀이 이루어지게 하려는 것이었다.
ko.B: 이것은 "아버지께서 저에게 주신 사람들 가운데 저는 하나도 잃지 않았습니다" 하신 그분의 말씀이 이루어지게 하려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 이렇게 해서 예수께서 전에 하신 말씀이 이루어졌다. "아버지께서 저에게 주신 사람들 가운데 저는 한 사람도 잃지 않았습니다."

decisions.choice: so that ... might be fulfilled: John's comment on why the disciples went free
decisions.reason: The sentence is the narrator's, not Jesus's. It hangs on verse 8: Jesus asked that his disciples be let go, and they were, so that his own word came true.

decisions.choice: the word he had said: 17:12, and the promise of 6:39 and 10:28
decisions.reason: John quotes freely what Jesus said in his prayer: "I guarded them, and not one of them was lost" (17:12), echoing 6:39, "that I should lose nothing of all that he has given me". "Fulfilled" is the word John uses for Scripture coming true (12:38; 13:18; 17:12; 19:24, 36); here he uses it of Jesus's own word, as again in 18:32.

decisions.choice: I did not lose one: their safety at the arrest is part of Jesus's keeping of them
alternatives: only their physical safety that night
only their eternal safety, with no reference to that night
decisions.reason: In 6:39 and 17:12 not losing them means keeping them for eternal life. John applies the words to their escape from arrest. The two belong together: had the disciples been arrested with him that night, they might not have held out, as Peter's denials show (18:17, 25-27); Jesus keeps them in body so that they are kept for the life he promised.

decisions.choice: [This was] (L); This was so that his own word (B); This happened ... Jesus (R); lose / lost (every level)
alternatives: so that the word might be fulfilled (with no subject)
decisions.reason: English needs a subject for the purpose clause, supplied in brackets at Literal. Readable names Jesus, since the "he" could be misread, and says "come true" for "be fulfilled". Every level uses "lose", as at 6:39 and in the Balanced and Readable text of 17:12, so the reader hears the earlier word. The "you" is the Father and "me" is Jesus, so both take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: Cha ... Con in the quoted saying
decisions.reason: The words quoted are from Jesus's prayer to the Father (17:12), so they keep the "Cha" and "Con" of John 17.

decisions.choice: The quoted words keep the formal polite style (합쇼체) and 저 of Jesus's prayer
decisions.reason: The words quoted are from the prayer to the Father (17:12), which Korean gives in 합쇼체; quoting them the same way keeps the link.

source.text: Σίμων οὖν Πέτρος ἔχων μάχαιραν εἵλκυσεν αὐτὴν καὶ ἔπαισεν τὸν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως δοῦλον καὶ ἀπέκοψεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτάριον τὸ δεξιόν.

ko.B: 시몬 베드로는 칼을 가지고 있었다. 그는 칼을 빼어 대제사장의 종을 내리쳐서 오른쪽 귀를 잘라 버렸다.
ko.R: 시몬 베드로는 칼을 하나 가지고 있었다. 그는 칼을 빼서 대제사장의 종에게 휘둘렀다. 그 칼에 그 사람의 오른쪽 귀가 잘려 나갔다.

decisions.choice: a sword: a short sword or long knife carried for protection
alternatives: a large knife for cutting food
decisions.reason: The word is used of a short sword or a large knife. Men traveling at night might carry one; Luke records that the disciples had two (Luke 22:38). Peter draws it to defend Jesus, against what Jesus has just done in giving himself up (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the high priest's slave: a slave of Caiaphas's household, sent with the arresting party
decisions.reason: The word means a slave, a person owned by another. A high priest's slave might hold a trusted place in his household and act for his master, as this one seems to have done in the arrest. The high priest that year was Caiaphas (verse 13). Another slave of the household, a relative of this man, will recognize Peter (18:26).

decisions.choice: his right ear: all four Gospels tell of it; John alone names Peter and the slave
decisions.reason: Matthew, Mark and Luke each tell that one of those with Jesus cut off the ear of the high priest's slave (Matthew 26:51; Mark 14:47; Luke 22:50). Luke and John say it was the right ear, and Luke adds that Jesus healed it (Luke 22:51). The word for ear is a small form of the usual word, but in the speech of the time it meant simply the ear; it need not mean only the lobe.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: Simon Peter had a sword. He pulled it out ... (B, R); swung it at (R)
alternatives: having a sword, drew it and struck (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the participle into short sentences, as English tells an action. Readable says "swung it at" for "struck", since the blow cut off an ear rather than wounding him elsewhere.

decisions.choice: l’esclave (L); le serviteur (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for this word: Literal keeps "esclave"; Balanced and Readable say "serviteur", as the English says "servant", since the man's place in the household, not slavery itself, is the point here (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: 종 for doulos at every level
decisions.reason: The guide keeps 종 for doulos throughout; it covers a household slave or servant without the harsher 노예.

source.text: ἦν δὲ ὄνομα τῷ δούλῳ Μάλχος.

records.literal_gloss: Was now name to the slave Malchus.

en.L: Now the name of the slave was Malchus.

fr.L: Or le nom de l’esclave était Malchus.

vi.L: Vả, tên của người nô lệ là Man-chu.
vi.B: Người đầy tớ ấy tên là Man-chu.
vi.R: Người đầy tớ ấy tên là Man-chu.

decisions.choice: Malchus: a name used in the region in that period
decisions.reason: The name is found in the region in that period, among Nabateans and others, and is related to the Semitic word for "king". John alone gives it, and he refers to the man again in 18:26, where a relative of his speaks to Peter. Such details suggest that the writer knew the high priest's household (18:15-16).

decisions.choice: the name of the slave was (L); The servant's name was (B, R)
alternatives: There was a name to the slave
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the name to the slave was", a common way of giving a name; English says "his name was".

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: As in the first half of 18:10: "servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ Πέτρῳ· Βάλε τὴν μάχαιραν εἰς τὴν θήκην· τὸ ποτήριον ὃ δέδωκέν μοι ὁ πατὴρ οὐ μὴ πίω αὐτό;

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore the Jesus to the Peter, "Put the sword into the sheath; the cup which has given me the Father, not not shall I drink it?"

en.L: So Jesus said to Peter, "Put the sword into the sheath. The cup which the Father has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, shall I not drink it?"
en.B: Then Jesus told Peter, "Put your sword back in its sheath! Am I not to drink the cup that the Father has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.R: Jesus told Peter, "Put your sword away! The Father has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a cup of suffering to drink, and I will drink it."

fr.L: Jésus dit donc à Pierre : « Mets l’épée dans le fourreau ; la coupe que le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a donnée, ne la boirai-je pas ? »
fr.B: Alors Jésus dit à Pierre : « Remets ton épée au fourreau ! Ne vais-je pas boire la coupe que le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a donnée ? »
fr.R: Jésus a dit à Pierre : « Range ton épée ! Le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a donné une coupe de souffrance à boire, et je vais la boire. »

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu nói với Phi-e-rơ: "Hãy tra gươm vào vỏ. Chén mà Cha đã ban cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, lẽ nào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không uống sao?"
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu bảo Phi-e-rơ: "Hãy tra gươm vào vỏ! Chẳng lẽ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không uống chén mà Cha đã ban cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sao?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu bảo Phi-e-rơ: "Cất gươm đi! Cha đã trao cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chén đau khổ này, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ uống chén ấy."

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 베드로에게 말씀하셨다. "칼을 칼집에 꽂아라. 아버지께서 나에게 주신 잔을 내가 마시지 않겠느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 베드로에게 말씀하셨다. "네 칼을 칼집에 도로 꽂아라! 아버지께서 나에게 주신 잔을 내가 마시지 말아야 하겠느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 베드로에게 말씀하셨다. "칼을 집어넣어라! 아버지께서 나에게 고난의 잔을 주셨다. 나는 그 잔을 마실 것이다."

decisions.choice: shall I not drink it?: a question that expects "yes, I will"
alternatives: a real question, asking whether he should
decisions.reason: Greek uses two negatives together for the strongest denial; in a question they expect the answer "yes": of course he will drink it. Jesus is not weighing the choice. He has said his soul is troubled, yet he will not ask to be saved from this hour, for he came for it (12:27).

decisions.choice: the cup: the suffering and death the Father has given him; it may also recall the cup of God's judgment
alternatives: only the cup of suffering, with no thought of judgment
the cup of God's judgment as the main sense
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures a cup that God gives to drink can stand for what he appoints for a person, and often for his judgment (Psalm 75:9; Isaiah 51:17, 22; Jeremiah 25:15). In the other Gospels Jesus prays in the garden, "remove this cup from me; yet not what I will, but what you will" (Mark 14:36), and asks his disciples whether they can drink the cup he drinks (Mark 10:38). Here the cup is the suffering and death ahead of him. Whether John also means the cup of judgment, borne for others, he does not say. Marked uncertain on that point.

decisions.choice: the cup the Father has given me: Jesus receives his death from his Father, and Peter's sword stands in the way of it
decisions.reason: Jesus calls God "the Father" and speaks of his death as the Father's gift, using the same verb as in verse 9. Peter would fight to stop the arrest; Jesus will tell Pilate that his servants do not fight, because his kingdom is not from this world (18:36). The order to put the sword away is not only a rebuke but a choice to go the way the Father has given.

decisions.choice: your sword, its sheath (B); Put your sword away (R)
decisions.reason: Greek uses "the" where English says "your" and "its". Readable says simply "away".

decisions.choice: a cup of suffering; and I will drink it (a statement)
alternatives: the cup ... shall I not drink it? (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup stands for, keeping to the part that is certain (meaning decision m2), and turns the question into the statement it expects (meaning decision m1).

source.text: Ἡ οὖν σπεῖρα καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται τῶν Ἰουδαίων συνέλαβον τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἔδησαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἤγαγον πρὸς Ἅνναν πρῶτον· ἦν γὰρ πενθερὸς τοῦ Καϊάφα, ὃς ἦν ἀρχιερεὺς τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου·

records.literal_gloss: The therefore cohort and the commander-of-a-thousand and the officers of the Jews seized the Jesus and bound him, \v 13 and led [him] to Annas first; was for father-in-law of the Caiaphas, who was high priest of the year that;

en.L: So the cohort and the commander and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 13 and they led [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] to Annas first; for he was father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
en.B: Then the detachment of soldiers with its commander, and the temple police sent by the Jewish leaders, arrested Jesus and tied {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up. \v 13 They took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} first to Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
en.R: Then the Roman soldiers and their commander, together with the temple guards of the Jewish leaders, arrested Jesus. They tied {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up \v 13 and took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} first to Annas. Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was the high priest that year.

fr.L: La cohorte donc, et le commandant, et les gardes des Juifs saisirent Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} lièrent, \v 13 et ils [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] conduisirent d’abord chez Anne ; car il était le beau-père de Caïphe, qui était grand prêtre cette année-là.
fr.B: Alors le détachement de soldats et son commandant, avec les gardes du temple envoyés par les chefs juifs, arrêtèrent Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ligotèrent. \v 13 Ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmenèrent d’abord chez Anne, le beau-père de Caïphe, qui était grand prêtre cette année-là.
fr.R: Alors les soldats romains et leur commandant, avec les gardes du temple des chefs juifs, ont arrêté Jésus. Ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont ligoté \v 13 et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont emmené d’abord chez Anne. Anne était le beau-père de Caïphe, qui était le grand prêtre cette année-là.

vi.L: Vậy đội quân, viên chỉ huy nghìn quân và các cảnh vệ của người Do Thái bắt Đức Giê-xu và trói {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại, \v 13 và giải [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] đến An-ne trước; vì ông là cha vợ của Cai-phe, người làm thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm năm ấy.
vi.B: Bấy giờ toán lính cùng viên chỉ huy và lính canh đền thờ của các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái bắt Đức Giê-xu và trói {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại. \v 13 Họ giải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến An-ne trước, là cha vợ của Cai-phe, thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm năm ấy.
vi.R: Bấy giờ toán lính La Mã và viên chỉ huy của họ, cùng với lính canh đền thờ của các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái, bắt Đức Giê-xu. Họ trói {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại \v 13 và giải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến An-ne trước. An-ne là cha vợ của Cai-phe, thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm năm ấy.

ko.L: 그래서 부대와 천부장과 유대인들의 경비병들이 예수를 붙잡아 결박하고, \v 13 먼저 안나스에게로 [그분을] 끌고 갔다. 그는 그해의 대제사장인 가야바의 장인이었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러자 로마 군인들과 그 지휘관과 유대 지도자들이 보낸 성전 경비병들이 예수를 체포하여 묶었다. \v 13 그리고 그분을 먼저 안나스에게 끌고 갔다. 안나스는 그해의 대제사장인 가야바의 장인이었다.
ko.R: 그러자 로마 군인들과 그 지휘관과 유대 지도자들의 성전 경비병들이 예수님을 붙잡아 묶었다. \v 13 그리고 먼저 안나스에게 끌고 갔다. 안나스는 그해에 대제사장이던 가야바의 장인이었다.

decisions.choice: the cohort and the commander: Roman soldiers under their tribune
alternatives: the commander of the temple guard
decisions.reason: The word χιλίαρχος means "commander of a thousand". It was the Greek name for a Roman tribune, the officer over a cohort, and Acts uses it of the tribune of the Roman garrison in Jerusalem (Acts 21:31-33; 22:24). With "the cohort" (meaning decision m1 at verse 3) it shows that Roman soldiers took part in the arrest along with the temple police.

decisions.choice: the officers of the Jews: the temple police of the Jewish authorities
decisions.reason: These are the officers sent by the chief priests and the Pharisees (verse 3; 7:32, 45). "Of the Jews" names the Jewish authorities they served, set beside the Roman soldiers and their commander. It does not mean the Jewish people as a whole: Jesus and his disciples are Jews.

decisions.choice: Annas first: the former high priest, still powerful through his family, questioned Jesus before Caiaphas did
decisions.reason: Annas was high priest from AD 6 to 15, when the Romans removed him. The historian Josephus records that five of his sons held the office after him, and Caiaphas, the high priest in this year, was his son-in-law. Luke and Acts still call him high priest alongside Caiaphas (Luke 3:2; Acts 4:6). "First" looks ahead: after questioning Jesus, Annas sends him to Caiaphas (18:24).

decisions.choice: high priest that year: the year of Jesus's death
alternatives: the office changed hands every year
decisions.reason: As in 11:49 and 11:51 (meaning decision m1 at 11:49): Caiaphas held the office for many years, and "that year" marks the year in which Jesus died.

decisions.choice: seized and bound him: arrested him as a prisoner
decisions.reason: The first verb is the ordinary word for arresting someone; the second is "tie up". Jesus is led away bound, and Annas later sends him to Caiaphas still bound (18:24).

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms and meaning decision m2). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: the cohort, the commander, the officers (L); the detachment of soldiers, its commander, the temple police (B); the Roman soldiers, their commander, the temple guards (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 3 (rendering decision r-en-2 there). Every level says "commander", which is what the title meant; "tribune" is the Roman name for the rank (meaning decision m1). Readable breaks the long sentence, ending the first part after "arrested Jesus" so that verse 13 begins at "and took him".

decisions.choice: les gardes des Juifs (L); les gardes du temple envoyés par les chefs juifs (B); les gardes du temple des chefs juifs (R); aux chefs juifs (B, R) in verse 14
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: Literal keeps the word John wrote, and Balanced and Readable name the authorities the officers served (meaning decision m2), since French "les Juifs" alone reads as the whole people. Jesus and his disciples are Jews. In verse 14 the word means the members of the council, and Balanced and Readable say "les chefs juifs" there too.

decisions.choice: người Do Thái (L); các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's rendering of "the Jews" where the authorities are meant, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: viên chỉ huy nghìn quân
decisions.reason: Literal gives the sense of the Greek title, commander of a thousand; Balanced and Readable say "viên chỉ huy".

decisions.choice: 천부장 (L); 지휘관 (B, R) for chiliarchos
decisions.reason: 천부장 ("commander of a thousand") is the established word and keeps the Greek title at Literal; Balanced and Readable use the plain word for an officer in command.

source.text: ἦν δὲ Καϊάφας ὁ συμβουλεύσας τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὅτι συμφέρει ἕνα ἄνθρωπον ἀποθανεῖν ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Was now Caiaphas the [one] having advised the Jews that it is profitable one man to die for the people.

en.L: Now Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it is better for one man to die for the people.
en.B: It was Caiaphas who had advised the Jewish leaders that it would be better for one man to die for the people.
en.R: Caiaphas was the one who had told the Jewish leaders it would be best to let one man die for the people.

fr.L: Or Caïphe était celui qui avait conseillé aux Juifs qu’il est avantageux qu’un seul homme meure pour le peuple.
fr.B: C’était Caïphe qui avait donné ce conseil aux chefs juifs : il valait mieux qu’un seul homme meure pour le peuple.
fr.R: Caïphe était celui qui avait dit aux chefs juifs qu’il valait mieux laisser mourir un seul homme pour le peuple.

vi.L: Vả, Cai-phe là người đã khuyên người Do Thái rằng một người chết thay cho dân thì có lợi hơn.
vi.B: Chính Cai-phe là người đã khuyên các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái rằng thà để một người chết thay cho dân thì có lợi hơn.
vi.R: Cai-phe là người đã bảo các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái rằng tốt nhất là để một người chết thay cho cả dân.

ko.L: 가야바는 한 사람이 백성을 위하여 죽는 것이 유익하다고 유대인들에게 조언했던 사람이다.
ko.B: 가야바는 한 사람이 백성을 위해 죽는 것이 더 이롭다고 유대 지도자들에게 조언했던 사람이다.
ko.R: 가야바는 전에 유대 지도자들에게, 한 사람을 백성을 위해 죽게 하는 것이 가장 좋다고 말했던 사람이다.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the members of the council, the chief priests and the Pharisees
decisions.reason: John points back to the meeting of the council in 11:47-53, where Caiaphas spoke to the chief priests and Pharisees gathered there. These are the authorities, not the people as a whole.

decisions.choice: John reminds the reader of Caiaphas's advice in 11:49-52: the man before whom Jesus will stand has already decided that he must die
decisions.reason: The words repeat 11:50 almost exactly, without "for you". Caiaphas meant a political calculation: one man's death to spare the nation. John has said that, as high priest that year, he prophesied without knowing it that Jesus would die for the nation and for the scattered children of God (11:51-52). The outcome of the questioning that follows is already settled.

decisions.choice: it is better ... for the people: to their advantage; on their behalf and in their place
decisions.reason: The verb means "it is profitable" or "it is to someone's advantage", as in 11:50. "For" means on behalf of, and here also instead of (meaning decision m3 at 11:50).

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms and meaning decision m1). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: it is better (L); it would be better (B); it would be best to let (R); one man ... die for the people (every level)
alternatives: it is to your advantage (as at 11:50)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "one man" and "die for the people", the words of 11:50, so that the reader hears the echo. Here the Greek has no "for you", so "better" gives the sense of advantage plainly. Balanced and Readable use "would be", as English does in reported advice; Literal keeps the present tense of the original words.

decisions.choice: người Do Thái (L); các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 18:12: the members of the council are meant.

decisions.choice: 유익하다 (L); 더 이롭다 (B)
decisions.reason: The same words as Caiaphas's advice in 11:50, where the Korean has 유익하다 (L) and 이롭다 (B), so the reader hears the echo.
